dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Hmm. I wonder how this tea will taste.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: I asked someone to buy a few bags of good tea leaves from Fontaine. Quite the pricey purchase, if I might say so.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: I've long heard of the differences in water and soil makeup between Fontaine and Liyue, so I've been curious as to the flavors tea leaves from the former will produce.

choices.text: Why don't you also get some water from there?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Hmm... You do have a point. Though as the ancients say, "living waters silt once drawn."

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Were we to fetch water from Fontaine, the turbulent, tiring journey may rob the liquid of its flavor, rendering the resultant tea lesser as a result.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Is there really that much to getting water?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: To brew a good cup of tea is no less demanding a task than organizing an army for battle, along with all the elements that entails.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Buying good tea leaves is akin to elevating a wise and capable general to command.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Yet if the water and tea set are lacking, and if perhaps even the climate and weather not suitable...

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Then no matter how outstanding the general, if burdened with incompetent officers and feckless soldiery, the battle will surely be lost.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: As such, rather than chasing distant solutions, it would be better to simply brew this tea with some spring water from Liyue.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Perhaps the blend of two natures might produce a unique flavor all its own.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Ah. It should be about ready. Try some, if you would.

choices.text: That might be a more interesting approach.
